confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors are based on web searches of aggregated cost-of-living data. Expatica's Numbeo-derived June 2026 averages were about EUR 18.74 for an inexpensive meal, EUR 65 for a three-course mid-range meal for two, EUR 2.12 for a cappuccino and EUR 3.38 for a 0.5 L domestic draught beer. Citycost's October 2026 figure for the mid-range meal was about EUR 63, and MyLifeElsewhere's figures were similar. The beer anchor is about EUR 3.5 for a 0.5 L draught, the Numbeo-style serving. A local caña or zurito is smaller and cheaper. The cocktail anchor is about EUR 9.5, between Expatistan's thinly sampled EUR 10 club figure and one bar's listed EUR 8-8.50. The wine anchor is about EUR 3.8, based on guide ranges of roughly EUR 3-7 for wine and txakoli in pintxos bars, so it is less certain. Euros were converted to US dollars at about 1.10 USD per EUR, worked out from the RBA's 18 Nov 2026 AUD rates (0.6720 USD and 0.6115 EUR). Food prices were lifted slightly for the July 2026 pricing window. The four accommodation anchors come from general knowledge only, not booking searches or listings. They assume July peak-season demand in a city with limited hostel supply, so they are the least certain anchors. The RBA rate of 0.6720 for 18 Nov 2026 came from search results that pointed to the official RBA exchange-rates page. I did not open the page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Bilbao is among Spain's more expensive cities, about 10% above the national average and roughly 15% higher for restaurants, according to MyLifeElsewhere. Restaurant prices are similar to San Sebastián's lower end and Madrid. Accommodation is benchmarked against mid-sized northern Spanish and Basque cities in summer, below San Sebastián's peak-season rates.
